bark_origin: sRGB, like every colour value; the engine works linearly and converts in clients/AppWalk.cpp. Linear that gives 0.674/0.638/0.570. Measured bark reflectance in the visible is 0.05...0.25 for the native species and 0.45...0.60 for Betula — unconverted, every one of these sixteen numbers would be two to four times too bright.
name: birch
form_origin: derived from the habit this file used to state in prose and nothing read: "slender trunk, open airy crown, fine pendulous twigs (pendula)". crown is the envelope generators/GrowthForm.h scales by spread_m; bole_frac is the retired bare_steps over trunk_steps (9/30), so the clear stem, where branching starts and where the envelope's own t=0 sits are now one number instead of three. The retired `conical` was a cone-only special case of the envelope and is gone with it.
dbh_cm_origin: derived: DBH = height_m / (H/D) with H/D = 0.85. H/D is the forestry slenderness ratio, height in m over DBH in cm; silver birch, a pioneer, slender and short-lived. 22 / 0.85 = 25.9 cm, rounded to 26.
lai_origin: [SET] leaf area index, one-sided leaf area per m2 of crown projection. birch, a light-demanding species with a very open crown. It sets the card size: lai * crown projection = card count * leaves per card * lamina area * L^2.
min_radius_origin: derived: min_radius = base_radius / 160. 160 is the measured ratio of trunk-foot radius to terminal-shoot radius on a mature tree (0.24 m to 0.0015 m). The previous value was base_radius/16, i.e. a 3 cm branch as the finest shoot; TreeGrower::SpawnLateral discards every branch with order_radius*r <= min_radius, so growth ended two orders too early and the leaf area index at the rig read 0.39 instead of 6.0 (measured, beech).
max_order_origin: [SET] branching orders above the trunk. Five is the Strahler order of a mature crown; three never produced the outermost shoots at all.
